author: c2-sql-sme-critic (independent PostgreSQL SME critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; reviewed commit 8a7daa17)

findings.claim: GIFT item 'o1 the ON condition': the feedback on ON books.author_id = books.author_id says it pairs every author with every book. A book whose author_id is NULL pairs with no author, because NULL = NULL yields null, not true. This is the NULL rule the module teaches. The sentence holds only when author_id is never NULL.

evidence.section: PostgreSQL 19 (current): 9.2 Comparison Functions and Operators: "Ordinary comparison operators yield null (signifying 'unknown'), not true or false, when either input is null."

findings.recommendation: Say 'so every author pairs with every book that has an author_id', or 'ON is true for every book with an author_id, whatever author is on the other side'.

findings.claim: Shared SQLCHK.explain, branch 'column reference ... is ambiguous': the advice always uses alias s ('for example s.instructor_id'). On this page the ambiguous column is usually instructor_id, between the aliases c and i, and courses or instructors have no alias s. An unqualified ORDER BY instructor_id in Activity 3 produces this ERROR, and the advice then suggests an alias that the query does not define. A learner who follows it literally gets ERROR: missing FROM-clause entry for table "s".

evidence.section: PostgreSQL 19 (current): 7.2.1.2 Table and Column Aliases: "The alias becomes the new name of the table reference so far as the current query is concerned"

findings.recommendation: Write 'for example <alias>.instructor_id, using the alias you gave that table', or take the alias from the failing statement's FROM items.
